reason: The text depicts regular people (Naaman's servants and the captive girl) as supportive and respectful toward their leaders, not antagonistic. When Naaman becomes angry at Elisha's instructions, his servants respectfully approach him and persuade him to obey, saying 'My father, if the prophet had bid thee do some great thing, wouldest thou not have done it?' The young captive girl from Israel speaks favorably of the prophet Elisha to her mistress. The only antagonism present is Naaman's initial resistance to the prophet's instructions (though Naaman himself is a leader, not a regular person), which is quickly overcome. There is no evidence of regular people expressing antagonism toward their leaders throughout the passage.
